BITUMEN EMULSION FOR ROAD MAINTENANCE, SURFACE TREATMENT, AND COLD RECYCLING.

PetroBind supplies 21 emulsion grades spanning both anionic (SS, MS, RS) and cationic (CSS, CMS, CRS, K-class) chemistries. Because emulsion shelf-life, aggregate compatibility, and break-time are all job-specific, buyers should request grade confirmation and a data sheet/COA before committing to drums or bulk IBC shipments.

Bitumen emulsion is a liquid dispersion of bitumen in water with emulsifying agents, used where lower-temperature application, spraying, tack coats, prime coats, maintenance works, and surface treatments are preferred. PetroBind can quote anionic and cationic grades subject to destination, quantity, and logistics requirements.

APPLICATIONS

Tack coat, prime coat, slurry seal, surface dressing, cold mix, cape seal, fog seal, and pavement maintenance works.

PACKING

HDPE drums, IBC tanks, ISO tanks, and bulk tankers depending on quantity, destination, and project handling requirements. Emulsions are temperature and UV-sensitive; insulated ISO tanks or shaded container shipments recommended for tropical routes.

DOCUMENTS

COA, PDS, SDS/MSDS, sieve analysis, residue by distillation, particle charge, storage stability by confirmed grade and batch.

PROCUREMENT

Quoted only by RFQ: emulsion stability, shelf-life, route duration, and destination handling requirements need to be checked per lot.

EMULSION CLASSIFICATION

7 CLASSES ACROSS ANIONIC AND CATIONIC CHEMISTRIES.

Each class is engineered for a specific break-speed (slow, medium, rapid, quick-set) and electric surface charge. Cationic emulsions bond better to siliceous aggregates; anionic emulsions perform better on calcareous (limestone) aggregate. PetroBind export quotations include a particle-charge check against your project aggregate data when provided.

ANIONIC (–) — 3 CHARGE-MATCHED CLASSES
SS

SLOW SET

Slurry seal, microsurfacing, cold recycling mixes, and stockpile mixes. SS-1, SS-1h common.

MS

MEDIUM SET

Surface dressing, chip seals, and open-graded mixes. MS-1, HFMS-1, HFMS-2 in this range.

RS

RAPID SET

Tack coat and rapid-bond applications where quick break is required. RS-1, RS-2.

CATIONIC (+) — 4 CHARGE-MATCHED CLASSES
CSS

CATIONIC SLOW SET

Slurry seal, microsurfacing, and cold-in-place recycling. CSS-1, CSS-1h with siliceous aggregate bond.

CMS

CATIONIC MEDIUM SET

Aggregate surface dressing and seal coats. CMS-2, CMS-2h for coated macadam applications.

CRS

CATIONIC RAPID SET

Prime and tack coat on granular and asphalt bases. CRS-1, CRS-2 for rapid-break tack and prime work.

K

K-CLASS (QUICK BREAK)

K1-40, K1-60, K1-70, K2, K3 for fast-break tack coats, fog seals, and patching.

APPLICATION MATRIX
GRADE BY PAVEMENT WORK TYPE

Use this as a starting selection matrix. Final grade and residual binder content depend on aggregate mineralogy, climate, traffic class, and plant mixing protocol — confirm with PetroBind's technical desk before RFQ.

APPLICATION TYPICAL GRADES NOTES
TACK COAT (BOND COAT) CRS-1, CRS-2, RS-1, K1-60 Sprayed between asphalt layers to reduce slippage cracking. Typical rate 0.2–0.5 L/m² — confirm with the mix designer.
PRIME COAT SS-1 (diluted), CSS-1 Applied to a granular base before the first asphalt layer to bind the surface fines.
SURFACE DRESSING (CHIP SEAL) CRS-2, RS-2, HFRS-2 Emulsion plus aggregate chippings, rolled and cured; single or multiple seals.
SLURRY SEAL / MICROSURFACING CSS-1h, CQS-1h, QS-1h Graded aggregate, mineral filler, water and emulsion, machine-laid.
COLD MIX / COLD-IN-PLACE RECYCLING CMS-2, CMS-2h, HFMS-2 Reclaimed asphalt pavement blended with emulsion for patching and full-depth reclamation.
FOG SEAL / REJUVENATOR SS-1 (diluted), SS-1h, CSS-1h Light spray on aged asphalt to seal hairline cracks and restore surface flexibility.
POTHOLE PATCHING & TRENCH REPAIR CRS-1, CRS-2, K3 Quick-breaking emulsion patching mixes for utility cuts and winter maintenance.

AVAILABLE PRODUCT LIST

21 CATIONIC AND ANIONIC EMULSION GRADES QUOTED BY RFQ.

Each grade page lists typical penetration, softening point, residue, and standard ASTM/EN values. Because emulsions are produced per-batch, the Certificate of Analysis (COA) on your specific lot always takes precedence. Indicative typical values can be shared with an RFQ response.
